response.markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a small SASRec extension with measurable ranking benefits rather than a new encoder. All improvements below are hypotheses.

**Insights.** Starting-point evidence yields three insights: (1) Electronics has 14.95% sampled wrong ranks and a −0.4812 lower-decile margin, motivating stronger candidate discrimination. These training diagnostics do not establish validation performance. (2) Users report stale interests overriding current purpose. A separate recent-history representation could expose that distinction explicitly. (3) Broad associations dilute specific matches, while embedding similarity is near its neutral baseline. Collapsing representations are therefore not an established explanation, and stronger discrimination deserves priority over diversity penalties.

Related work supplies three insights: (1) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) motivates testing multiple negatives and calibrated objectives. Its recommended settings remain experimental starting points here. (2) [R²NS](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) motivates delaying hard sampling. Uniform negatives offer a simpler initial experiment with fewer false-negative assumptions. (3) [Teddy](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipm.2023.103619) motivates separating dominant and scattered interests. This supports testing distinct history summaries without claiming they recover true intent.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Constrained experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate discrimination | gSASRec calibration | Uniform multi-negative gBCE |
| Current-purpose modeling | Teddy interest separation | Gated recent-history residual |
| Behavioral succession | TGCL4SR transition graph | Training-only transition residual |

**Ideas and assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-negative gBCE | 3/7/4/9/2 | Established, inexpensive ranking intervention | Does not explicitly resolve stale interests |
| Gated recent-history residual with multi-negative ranking | 5/8/8/8/4 | Directly targets stale influence and weak immediate specificity | Recent interactions may represent completed purchases |
| Directed transition residual | 4/7/6/7/4 | Adds observed succession beyond textual association | Sparse transitions can reinforce popularity |

**Selected idea.** Add a gated recent-history residual to SASRec and train with uniform multi-negative sampled softmax. The recent branch targets two reported failures: historical interests overriding current purpose, and broad associations displacing specific recent matches. Candidate competition targets weak positive–negative separation, especially in Electronics; semantic compatibility remains unverified.

For every valid prefix, compute SASRec state h, mean embedding r of its last k nonpadding items, gate g= sigmoid(MLP([h,r])), and z=LayerNorm(h+g·Wr). Optimize cross-entropy over its next item and sampled negatives, excluding known training positives. Compare baseline, objective-only, branch-only, and combined variants under equal GPU caps.

Keep four-category routing, seeds, splits, and DATA_DIR unchanged. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10 within the shared budget. Save architecture settings and update the predictor writer. Preserve diagnostic interfaces, measure effective ranking margins, and mark unavailable category breakdowns explicitly.

idea.description: Extend each per-dataset SASRec with a gated recent-history residual and uniform multi-negative sampled-softmax training. This is a proposed experiment, with no measured improvement claimed.
idea.motivation: The recent branch explicitly addresses stale historical influence and broadly plausible recommendations crowding out specific current interests. Multi-negative competition addresses measured weak ranking separation, particularly Electronics' 14.95% sampled wrong-rank rate. Neither histories nor this architecture establish equipment compatibility or purchase satisfaction.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four datasets, and the existing split/evaluator contracts. Respect SASREC_EPOCHS with the supplied default of 200 and count all experiments against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Start with k=5 and 64 uniform negatives per valid position; these are proposed settings. Exclude padding, the target, and known training positives from negative sampling without consulting held-out labels; mask duplicate sampled candidates. Chunk candidate scoring when necessary. Compute recent summaries causally during training and identically during prediction. Save k, dimensions, gate parameters, normalization parameters, and model weights beneath the trial directory; update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the complete architecture and dataset routing. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Ensure view.model is the actual module and log2feats returns the effective gated features used by predict_score. Retain existing margin definitions and report unavailable metadata breakdowns as unavailable. Use only titles/descriptions if later text experiments are attempted; supplied generic rating/review examples do not authorize unavailable fields.
idea.pseudocode:
for dataset in four_categories:
    initialize SASRec and recent-residual parameters with training seed 42
    for batch within allocated training budget:
        h = SASRec.log2feats(sequence)
        r = causal_recent_mean(item_emb(sequence), window=5, ignore_padding=True)
        g = sigmoid(gate(concat(h, r)))
        z = layer_norm(h + g * project(r))
        for valid next-item positions in memory-bounded chunks:
            negatives = sample_uniform_items(exclude=known_training_positives_and_target)
            candidates = concat(target, negatives)
            logits = dot(z, item_emb(candidates))
            loss = cross_entropy(logits, target_index=0)
        update_parameters(loss)
    save_complete_checkpoint_and_predictor_configuration()
compare baseline, objective_only, branch_only, combined under comparable GPU caps
select using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 only

originality.positive: Combines an explicit recent-interest residual with candidate competition in a small, testable extension aligned with the observed failures.
originality.negative: Gated interest mixtures and sampled ranking objectives are established techniques; this is an adaptation rather than a new model family.

future_potential.positive: Provides a compact foundation for testing when recent behavior should override broader history, with interpretable ablations.
future_potential.negative: Recent behavior can reflect a satisfied need, and improved sampled ranking may not translate to immediate usefulness or validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses SASRec embeddings and encoder; the added pooling, projection, and gate require relatively little model code.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal pooling, efficient negative exclusion, checkpoint compatibility, and matching diagnostic/predictor behavior require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal sequence encoder and dot-product scoring baseline.
limitations: Does not guarantee that attention distinguishes current purpose from historical association.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Studies sampled-BCE overconfidence and proposes generalized BCE.
Motivates controlled experiments with more negative candidates.
limitations: Published settings are not established optima for the pinned benchmark.
Does not establish the proposed sampled-softmax and recent-residual combination.

related_work.title: R²NS
contributions: Combines uniform warm-up with progressively harder stochastic negative selection.
limitations: Adds sampling complexity and possible false negatives.
Reported results do not establish improvements under this evaluator.

related_work.title: Teddy
contributions: Models dominant trends and scattered interests through distinct representations.
limitations: Does not establish that a fixed recent window identifies current purpose or purchase saturation.

related_work.title: TGCL4SR
contributions: Combines a temporal item-transition graph, time-aware Transformer, and contrastive objectives.
limitations: Observed transitions do not provide verified complementarity or compatibility labels.
Its complete architecture adds complexity beyond the proposed initial experiment.
